## Gold: The Gilded Covenant (Tithers)
Pitch: Wealth is the true faith.
Verbs: gain, sponsor (mark a space), trade
Scoring: The Coffers. At round end, whoever holds the most gold gains followers: I 1 / II 2 / III 3 (ties: every tied player gains it). Game total at most 6.
Emits: gain (gold, often 3+ at once), give (Patronage), mark a space, hold the most of a color
Consumes: buy an item (recruit: Collection, Almoner), rivals taking spaces (Patronage), member count (Tithe, Banker)

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Tithe | +2 gold, +1 more for every 3 members you have. |
| I | Patronage | +1 gold. Mark an empty space: its taker and you each gain 1 gold. |
| I | Indulgence | Trade up to 3 resources for gold one-for-one, then +2 gold. |
| II | Usury | +1 gold for every 2 gold you hold (max +4). |
| II | Collection | +2 gold, +1 per member rivals recruited since your last turn. |
| III | Jubilee | Double your gold, up to +7. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fickle Donor | 1 | Release at any time: gain 2 gold. | 0 |
| Tithe-Taker | 2 | Tithe gives +1 more gold. | 0 |
| Moneylender | 3 | You may pay gold in place of any color when recruiting. | 0 |
| Almoner | 4 | Whenever a rival recruits a member, gain 1 gold. | 0 |
| Banker | 5 | At each round start, +1 gold per member you have. | +1 |
| Gilded Prophet | 7 | At game end, +1 follower per 2 gold you hold (max 5). | +1 |

Notes:
- Core tension: gold is both the Coffers score and your best currency (Moneylender). Every recruit paid in gold costs you Coffers standing. Gilded Prophet resolves the tension late: the hoard itself becomes followers.
- Fallback rule (L8): if Patronage finds no empty space (only the very last pick of round I), it gives +1 gold instead. Mark is a token on the wheel (L5 warn, same as v2).
- Values (u): Tithe 2 early / 3-4 late; Patronage 2 + rival 1 (spill 0.5); Indulgence ~2.3 (conversion + 2); Usury 3-4; Collection ~4 (2 + about 2 recruits since last turn, never dead); Jubilee 5-7 (capped, fixes uncapped Treasury). All in band.
- Members (price / total EV incl. 1.5u per follower): Donor 1/2 = 50%; Tithe-Taker 2/4 = 50%; Moneylender 3/5 = 60% (was 133% as once-per-round Broker's Scale); Almoner 4/6 = 67% (was 33% auto-buy at 3); Banker 5/7.5 = 67% (bought in R2: ~5 gold at R3 start + 2 followers); Gilded Prophet 7/~9.5 = ~74% for a gold hoarder (2 followers + ~4 from the hoard). This beats Garland's rate only if you commit to holding gold, which is the fix for 7-cost Favor items losing to fixtures.
- Dropped Vault (defensive item dangled with no taker on the wheel) and Guild Charter (trap).
- Silo index ~0.5: Usury/Jubilee compound gold, but Collection, Almoner and Patronage feed off the table.
- Lints: L1 pass (max 14), L2 pass, L3 pass, L4 n/a, L5 warn (mark token), L6 pass, L7 pass, L8 pass with fallback rule, L9 n/a, L10 pass (Gilded Prophet pays at game end, which is the final round end).

## Shadow: The Veiled Hand (Infiltrators)
Pitch: Topple the mighty from within.
Verbs: take (only from players ahead), share a space, sway (the leader only)
Scoring: Conspiracy. At round end, every player holding more shadow than the leader gains followers: I 1 / II 2 / III 3. The leader is whoever has the most followers before round-end scoring; with tied leaders, compare against the highest shadow among them. The leader never scores it. Game total per player at most 6.
Emits: take (from ahead), share a space, echo (Puppet Master), sway, recruit from any stall
Consumes: the leader / ahead-behind, occupied spaces, rivals' spaces (Puppet Master), rivals' members (Defection)

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Lurk | +1 shadow per player ahead of you, minimum 2. |
| I | Infiltrate | +1 shadow and 1 resource. Your next worker may share an occupied space. |
| I | Pilfer | +1 shadow. Take 1 resource from a player ahead of you (else +1 shadow). |
| II | Smuggle | +2 shadow. This turn, recruit from any stall, paying 1 less. |
| II | Blackmail | +1 shadow. Take 1 resource from each player ahead of you (none: +2 shadow). |
| III | Defection | +2 shadow. Sway a member costing ≤4 from the leader (else +3 shadow). |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sleeper Agent | 1 | Release at any time: take 2 resources from a player ahead of you. | 0 |
| Cat Burglar | 2 | Your workers may share occupied spaces in this sphere. | 0 |
| Fence | 3 | Whenever you take resources from a player, also gain 1 shadow. | 0 |
| Smuggler | 4 | You may recruit from any stall; when you do, +1 shadow. | 0 |
| Spymaster | 5 | At round end, before scoring, +1 shadow per player ahead of you. | +1 |
| Puppet Master | 7 | Once per round, echo a space a player ahead of you took. | +1 |

Notes:
- New scoring shape (a threshold against the leader rather than a majority): several players can win, nobody loses followers to it, and the leader can only blunt it by holding shadow, which drags the leader into this sphere. Fixes v2's L4 fail (Favor taken from second place). The leader is set before scoring, so the order of round-end payouts never matters.
- Shadow was weakest in v2. Every space is now in band: Lurk 2-3 (lures trailing players, scales as the table spreads); Infiltrate ~3 (1 + 1.2 + share option); Pilfer ~2.5 (fallback when leading); Smuggle ~4; Blackmail ~3.5 with a fallback; Defection ~6.5-8 (+2 shadow + a member worth ~1.5u follower + ability, plus the swing against the leader).
- Harm budget: it's small and only points up. Takes never exceed what a target holds (no one drops below 0). The one follower loss in the game is Defection: once per game, the leader only, with a cost cap that protects their capstone. Sway moves a member mid-round, but followers are tallied at round end, so L10 holds. Flag Defection for the playtest feel-check.
- Members: Sleeper 1/~2 = 50%; Cat Burglar 2/~3.5 = 57% (gets you into full round-I spaces of this sphere); Fence 3/4.5 = 67% (no longer adds harm, unlike v2's Dagger); Smuggler 4/~7 = 57% (was 133% as Smuggler's Map); Spymaster 5/7.5 = 67% (2 followers + Conspiracy insurance); Puppet Master 7/10-14 = 50-70% (copying the leader's best round-III space is the capstone burst; does nothing while you lead, which is intended).
- No pure defensive members, so nothing dangles when this sphere is off the wheel. Veil, Vault and Dagger are gone.
- Echo rule (global): an echo resolves a space's effect without placing a worker and can never copy an echo, so Puppet Master can't chain.
- Lints: L1 pass, L2 pass ("this sphere" means the member's own sphere), L3 pass (Pilfer only reaches up), L4 pass, L5 pass (Infiltrate needs two workers on one space, warn as in v2), L6 pass, L7 pass, L8 pass (every space has a fallback), L9 pass, L10 pass.

## Verdant: The Evergreen Circle (Ritualists)
Pitch: Every rite returns, renewed.
Verbs: echo (repeat or copy, never an echo of an echo), plant
Scoring: The Rite. At round end, +1 follower per echo you made this round, max I 1 / II 2 / III 3. Any player's echoes count. Game total at most 6.
Emits: echo, give (Mirror Twin)
Consumes: rivals' spaces (Mirror), rivals' members (Graft), echoes from any source (Rite, Tend)

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Tend | +2 verdant, or +3 if you've echoed this round. |
| I | Mirror | Echo a space a rival took this round (none yet: +2 verdant). |
| I | Plant | +1 verdant. Plant up to 2 resources; they return doubled at your next placement. |
| II | Return | Echo any space you took this round or last round. |
| II | Graft | Echo one ability of a rival's member (none: +3 verdant). |
| III | Renewal | Echo two spaces you took in earlier rounds. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seedling | 1 | At each round start, +1 verdant. | 0 |
| Gardener | 2 | You may plant 1 more resource. | 0 |
| Mirror Twin | 3 | When you echo a rival's space, you both gain 1 resource. | 0 |
| Circle Elder | 4 | Whenever you echo, also gain 1 resource of any color. | 0 |
| Timekeeper | 5 | Once per round, echo a round-I space right after you take it. | 0 |
| World Tree | 7 | Planting counts as an echo, and planted resources return tripled. | +2 |

Notes:
- Termination (fixes the v2 L9 fail): an echo can never copy a space or ability that is itself an echo. Renewal is capped at two spaces, and Timekeeper is once per round.
- The Rite now has ring caps (1/2/3), down from uncapped (~8+). Eternity (~20u) becomes Renewal: two earlier-round spaces, about 2.5 + 4 = 6.5u plus up to 2 followers inside the R3 cap, so ~9.5u. That's the top of the band and the intended round-III burst.
- Dead turns fixed: Mirror falls back when nobody has placed yet; Return reaches into last round, so it always has a target in round II and later; Graft falls back when rivals have no members. Plant has a +1 baseline and returns at your next placement (at round end if you have none left), so it still works in round III instead of paying out after the game ends.
- Values: Tend 2-3; Mirror ~2.5 + 1 follower the first time (~4, within +40% of band); Plant ~3; Return ~3.5 + follower; Graft ~3 + follower; Renewal ~9.5. Round-I echoes grow naturally because later rings hold bigger spaces to copy.
- Graft on a passive ability (e.g. paying in another color) applies it for this turn only. Flag as a UI clarity point.
- Members: Seedling 1/~2.5-3 = ~40% (cheap-recruit tier, intended); Gardener 2/3.5 = 57%; Mirror Twin 3/4.5 = 67% (self +1 per echo, spill ratio 1.0; v2's Echo Chamber gave the owner nothing); Circle Elder 4/~6.3 = 63%; Timekeeper 5/~8 = 62% (was a 40% auto-buy at 4 when it could echo any space); World Tree 7/~10 = 70% (3 followers + tripled plants + Rite ticks). Cuttings is cut: its only emitter was this sphere.
- Silo index ~0.55: Return and Renewal are self-echoes, while Mirror, Graft and Mirror Twin need the table.
- Lints: L1 pass, L2 pass, L3 pass, L4 n/a, L5 warn (planted tray on the panel, as in v2), L6 pass, L7 pass, L8 pass, L9 pass, L10 pass.

## Sunlight: The Radiant Choir (Evangelists)
Pitch: Give freely, gather the faithful.
Verbs: give, trade (convert colors), set
Scoring: Harmony. At round end, +1 follower per full set you hold (one of each wheel color), max I 1 / II 2 / III 3. Sets are counted, not spent. Game total at most 6.
Emits: give (Alms, Ascension), gain 3+ at once, set
Consumes: gives from any source (Missionary, and sets fill faster from rivals' gifts), gain 3+ (Witness), member count (Sun Prophet)

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Sermon | +2 sunlight, +1 more if you hold a full set. |
| I | Pilgrimage | +2 resources, each a different color. |
| I | Alms | +3 of one color. Each rival gains 1 of it. |
| II | Conversion | Convert any of your resources to other colors, then +2 of any color. |
| II | Revelation | +1 of every color. |
| III | Ascension | +2 of every color. Each rival gains 1 resource of their choice. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Novice | 1 | At each round start, +1 resource of a color you lack. | 0 |
| Pilgrim | 2 | Pilgrimage gives 1 more resource, of a third different color. | 0 |
| Witness | 3 | Whenever a rival gains 3 or more resources at once, gain 1 sunlight. | 0 |
| Missionary | 4 | Whenever your action gives rivals resources, gain 2 sunlight. | 0 |
| Halo Bearer | 5 | Counts as one of every color toward full sets. | +1 |
| Sun Prophet | 7 | At game end, +1 follower per 2 members you have. | +2 |

Notes:
- Charisma is generosity that converts people. Gifts spill onto the table, Conversion "switches" colors, and the capstone rewards the size of your following.
- Zenith's spill fixed: Ascension gives the actor 8u and the table 3u (spill ratio 0.375, was 1.5). Alms gives 3u to the actor and 3u to the table (ratio 1.0, at the limit, round I only).
- Values: Sermon 2-3; Pilgrimage 2.4; Alms 3 (+3 to the table); Conversion ~3.4 (2.4 + flexibility, no longer a flat swap); Revelation 4; Ascension 8. All in band. No space can be dead: each one gains something unconditionally.
- Harmony now has ring caps (1/2/3), so Halo Bearer and gifts help you reach the cap rather than run past it.
- Members: Novice 1/~2.7 = 37% (cheap-recruit tier, intended); Pilgrim 2/4 = 50% (was Lens at 100%); Witness 3/6 = 50% (about 9 triggers from round II); Missionary 4/~7.5 = 53% (fed by Alms, Ascension and any sphere that gives; replaces the 33% auto-buy Gift Basket); Halo Bearer 5/~6.5 = 77% (2 followers + about 2 Harmony ticks + Sermon bonus; watch it); Sun Prophet 7/~9.75 = 72% (3 followers + about 3.5 from a 7-member cult). It's a recruit-everything payoff that rewards the main loop instead of competing with Garland.
- Kaleidoscope is cut (trap). Interplay is generic throughout: colors, sets, gives, members.
- Lints: L1 pass, L2 pass, L3 pass (Alms spill is a lure, not a toll), L4 n/a, L5 pass, L6 pass, L7 pass, L8 pass, L9 n/a, L10 pass (Sun Prophet pays at game end, the final round end).

SET NOTES (all four):
- Links (emit → consume): recruit (all) → Collection, Almoner, Tithe, Sun Prophet; give (Patronage, Alms, Ascension, Mirror Twin) → Missionary, Harmony; gain 3+ (Tithe, Usury, Jubilee, Alms, Revelation, Ascension) → Witness; any rival's space → Mirror, Puppet Master; rival members → Graft, Defection; echo (Verdant + Puppet Master) → Rite, Tend; leader/ahead → Lurk, Pilfer, Blackmail, Conspiracy, Spymaster; occupied spaces → Infiltrate, Cat Burglar, Patronage. That's 9+ links, and every sphere both emits and consumes.
- Swap test: no defensive member is left to dangle. Every cross-sphere hook (recruit, give, gain 3+, spaces, members, leader) has emitters in at least 3 spheres. Echo outside Verdant comes only from Puppet Master, but the Rite is Verdant's own, so nothing breaks if either is absent.
- Scoring shapes: majority (Coffers), threshold against the leader (Conspiracy), per-event (Rite), set collection (Harmony). Each caps at 1/2/3, at most 6 followers per game, within the 25% contest budget.
- Each 7-cost capstone scales with its sphere's engine (gold hoard, copying the leader, tripled plants, cult size) rather than being a flat +2 Favor, so none is dominated by Garland or Diadem.
- Fixtures unchanged: Laurel 2→1, Garland 5→3, Diadem 8→6 (2 per player, game clock).

## Crimson: The Revival (Prophet)
Pitch: Outshine the faithful above you.
Verbs: preach (gain zeal, more in a crowd), sway (take from a player ahead), recruit
Scoring: SWAY. At round end, +1 follower for each player ahead of you who has less zeal than you, counting at most 2 such players. Ring values per player: I = 1 / II = 1 / III = 2. A leader with no one ahead scores the ring value once instead, if they hold the most zeal. Swayed followers come from the supply, so nobody loses Favor. (Shape: a pairwise comparison against those above you, not a majority.)
Emits: gain (zeal, including gains of 3 or more), give (Testify), take (Whisper takes zeal, Poach takes a member, both only from a player ahead), buy an item (an extra recruit), share a space (Sermon draws a crowd)
Consumes: ahead/behind (Pulpit, Sway, Poach, Herald, Fickle Convert), give (Hymnal Keeper), a rival's gain of 3 or more (Firebrand), share a space (Sermon), member count (Great Awakening)

| Ring | Action | Effect (14 words or fewer) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Sermon | +2 zeal, or +3 if a rival is already in this sphere. |
| I | Testify | +3 zeal. Give a rival 1 zeal from the supply. |
| I | Whisper | +1 zeal. Take 1 zeal from a player ahead (none ahead: +1 zeal). |
| II | Pulpit | +2 zeal, plus 1 per player ahead of you. |
| II | Poach | Extra recruit: any stall, or a player ahead's member (cost 4 or less), paying them. |
| III | Great Awakening | +3 zeal, plus 1 per member you have. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (14 words or fewer) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fickle Convert | 1 | At round end, it defects to a player behind you with more zeal. | 0 |
| Silver Tongue | 2 | Zeal ties count as out-zealing for you. | 0 |
| Hymnal Keeper | 3 | Whenever you give a rival anything, gain 1 zeal. | 0 |
| Firebrand | 4 | Whenever a rival gains 3 or more at once, gain 1 zeal. | 0 |
| Herald | 5 | Placing in this sphere: +2 zeal, and each rival behind you gains 1. | 0 |
| Hierophant | 6 | For Sway, your zeal counts double. | +2 |

Notes:
- Identity: the underdog preacher. Zeal is a real currency, so every unit you hold back for Sway at round end is a member you didn't recruit. Same spend-or-hold tension as the old gold contest, but compared player by player against whoever sits above you.
- How sway works under the principles: follower sway pays out from the supply (Favor goes down only rarely, and only from the leader). The real sway is of zeal (Whisper) and of members (Poach). Poach pays the victim the member's full cost, so the leader is forced to sell rather than robbed. That's small harm, aimed up, and even the victim gets paid.
- Poach is an extra recruit on top of your normal one-per-placement buy. Its stall-or-rival choice means it is never dead for the leader. A member transferred mid-round moves its follower, which is tallied at round end (consistent with L10).
- Fickle Convert: if several players behind you have more zeal, it goes to the one with the most (ties go to the one furthest behind). It resolves before the round-end tally. It's a cheap member with a built-in risk. If it is made loyal or otherwise protected from being taken, it stays put (a nice generic combo).
- Combos: Testify + Hymnal Keeper (the gift pays you back). Whisper both raises your zeal and lowers theirs, a 2-point swing in the Sway comparison. Silver Tongue + Hierophant lock up Sway late. Firebrand watches the table for big gains from any sphere. Great Awakening rewards a cult built over the game: the round-3 burst.
- Value pass (u): Sermon 2–3; Testify 3, with 1 spilled to a rival (spill 0.33); Whisper about 2.5 counting the swing; Pulpit 2–5, about 4 on average; Poach about 3.5–4 (2u for the extra buy, plus choice, plus a member that isn't on any stall); Great Awakening 7–9 late, at the top of the band.
- Member pricing (EV if bought at the start of round II, then cost as a share of EV): Fickle Convert about 1.5u (67%); Silver Tongue 1.5 + about 2 = 3.5 (57%); Hymnal Keeper 1.5 + about 4 = 5.5 (55%); Firebrand 1.5 + 12 triggers × 0.5 = 7.5 (53%); Herald 1.5 + 3 uses × 2 = 7.5 (67%; rivals behind gain about 1.5 per use, spill under 1); Hierophant 4.5 + about 3.5 = 8 (75%, a little rich for a capstone, which is deliberate since the bulk fixtures should win at the high end).
- Self-lint:
  - L1 pass (longest are Sermon, Whisper and Poach at 13 or fewer).
  - L2 pass (no other sphere named; zeal is this sphere's own resource).
  - L3 pass (no round-I cost).
  - L4 pass (takes only from a player ahead, and only when they have it; Poach compensates; Fickle Convert moves up the table only).
  - L5 pass (zeal counts are already on player panels; Sway reads off Favor order plus zeal).
  - L6 pass (Sway is the only source of followers).
  - L7 pass (3/2/1 spaces, 6 members).
  - L8 pass (Whisper and Poach have fallbacks).
  - L9 pass (no echoes; Hymnal Keeper fires on give, and Testify's gift isn't re-triggered).
  - L10 pass (Sway and Fickle Convert resolve at round end).
- Risks:
  - The Sway total can reach 2 + 2 + 4 = 8 followers in a game. That's just above the 6–7 contest guide, though about 4–5 is typical, so watch it.
  - Pulpit and Sway lean toward catch-up. The leader still has Sermon, Testify, Great Awakening and the leader clause, but check parity (Q8) in mind-play.

## Ivory: The Vigil (Zealot)
Pitch: Seal the faithful; they stay.
Verbs: pray (gain faith), consecrate (make a member loyal), offer (give to a rival for faith)
Scoring: VIGIL. At round end, +1 follower per loyal member you have, up to a cap of I = 1 / II = 2 / III = 4. (Shape: a personal capped holding count that everyone can score. No contest.)
Loyal (a seal on the member card): a loyal member can't be taken or released, and it counts for Vigil.
Emits: gain (faith; Ascension and Communion can be gains of 3 or more), give (Offering; Almsgiver's return gift), a release (Doubter), protection against take (loyal members), spill (Communion)
Consumes: take (Penitent; loyalty blocks it), give (Almsgiver), member count (Ascension), ahead (Penitent fires only on harm from a player ahead)

| Ring | Action | Effect (14 words or fewer) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Prayer | +2 faith, plus 1 per loyal member you have (max +2). |
| I | Consecrate | +2 faith. You may pay 2 faith to make a member loyal. |
| I | Offering | +2 faith. You may give a rival 1 resource for +2 more faith. |
| II | Sanctuary | Make a member loyal free, then +1 faith per loyal member (none: +2 faith). |
| II | Communion | Every player gains 1 faith per loyal member they have; you gain 2 more. |
| III | Ascension | +1 faith per member you have, then make 2 members loyal free. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (14 words or fewer) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Doubter | 1 | Can never be loyal. Release it anytime for 2 faith. | 0 |
| Bell-Ringer | 2 | Prayer gives +1 more faith. | 0 |
| Penitent | 3 | When a player ahead takes from you, gain 2 faith. | 0 |
| Almsgiver | 4 | When a rival gives you anything, gain 1 faith; they gain 1 faith too. | 0 |
| Abbess | 5 | Making a member loyal costs you no faith. | +1 |
| Saint | 7 | Arrives loyal. Your other members can't be taken. | +3 |

Notes:
- Identity: the patient zealot. While others race for zeal and coin, Ivory turns members into a sealed flock that pays a follower every round and can't be swayed away. Loyalty is the counter to any sphere that takes members or resources, but it's expressed generically: "can't be taken."
- The trade-off in loyalty: a loyal member can't be released either, so loyalty fights any release-for-resources hook on the wheel. Sealing is a commitment, not a free upgrade.
- Arc: round I seals 0–1 members (2 faith each). Round II's Sanctuary and Communion grow the flock. Ascension seals 2 more in round III, just as the Vigil cap jumps to 4: the burst. A Vigil player can reach about 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 followers, but only by recruiting broadly first, which feeds the main loop (buy lots of members).
- Combos:
  - Offering + Almsgiver (+ any "when you give" member in the pool): one gift sets off a small chain of thanks that ends, because gains aren't gives.
  - Saint + Fickle-style members: protection keeps a cheap risky member at home.
  - Penitent rewards the leader for being picked on, which softens feel-bad.
  - Communion is a warm spill that also pays rivals who dabbled in loyalty.
- Value pass (u): Prayer 2 early to 4 late; Consecrate about 2.5–3 (2 faith, or a 2u loyalty seal worth about 1–2 followers over the game plus protection); Offering 2–3, with 1 resource handed to a rival (spill 0.25); Sanctuary about 4–5; Communion about 4 for you at 2 loyal, about 1–3 spilled (ratio about 0.5–0.75); Ascension about 5 faith from members plus 2 seals (about 3u) = about 8, inside the band.
- Member pricing (EV if bought at the start of round II, then cost as a share of EV): Doubter about 1.5–2u (50–67%); Bell-Ringer 1.5 + about 2.5 = 4 (50%); Penitent 1.5 + about 4 = 5.5 (55%, situational, best for whoever is ahead); Almsgiver 1.5 + about 4 triggers × 1.25 = 6.5 (62%); Abbess 3 + about 4 saved = 7 (71%); Saint 6 + loyal Vigil about 1.5 + protection about 1 = 8.5 (82%, a capstone trailing the Diadem on purpose).
- Self-lint:
  - L1 pass (Sanctuary and Communion are both 14).
  - L2 pass ("loyal" is defined on this sphere; other spheres need only the generic "take" and "release").
  - L3 pass (every round-I cost is optional: Consecrate's payment, Offering's gift).
  - L4 pass (no harm emitted).
  - L5 pass (loyalty is a seal icon on the member card; the Vigil cap is printed per ring).
  - L6 pass (Vigil is the only source of followers).
  - L7 pass (3/2/1 spaces, 6 members).
  - L8 warn → pass (Consecrate with no members still gives 2 faith; Sanctuary has its fallback).
  - L9 pass (Almsgiver's return is a gain, not a give, so it can't loop).
  - L10 pass (Vigil pays at round end; Doubter's release removes a follower, tallied at round end).
- Risks:
  - Silo index may sit near 0.6, since loyalty compounds within the sphere. Penitent, Almsgiver, Offering and Communion are the table hooks; check in the interplay graph.
  - Communion's spill can exceed 1 if rivals hold many loyal members. Cap it or keep it as a feature if mind-play shows it's rare.

## Crimson: The Pyre (Martyr)
Pitch: Burn members, blaze brighter.
Verbs: release, kindle (gain ember)
Scoring: **Ashes**: at round end, +1 follower for each member you released this round, up to 1 / 2 / 3 (rings I / II / III). Per-event, capped. Game max 6.
Emits: release (by anyone's choice, public), gain 3+ at once (Bonfire, Conflagration), recruit (Phoenix free recruit, Ferryman trade-in), give (Herald of Ash spill), stall churn (released members leave, stalls refill)
Consumes: releases by anyone (Vigil, Mourner), member count (Kindle), cheap recruits (Lamplighter)

Resource: ember. Released members leave the game (base rule for the generic cult verb).

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Kindle | +2 ember, plus 1 per 2 members you have. |
| I | Offering | Release a member for its cost +1 in any colors, or gain 2 ember. |
| I | Vigil | +1 ember, plus 1 per member released this round by anyone. |
| II | Bonfire | Release a member for its cost +3 in any colors, or gain 3 ember. |
| II | Phoenix | Release a member; recruit one free costing at most 2 more. Else +3 ember. |
| III | Conflagration | Release up to 3 members for 3 any colors each, or gain 6 ember. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moth | 1 | When released, gain 1 ember. | 0 |
| Mourner | 2 | When a rival releases a member, gain 1 ember. | 0 |
| Lamplighter | 3 | When you recruit a member costing 2 or less, gain 1 ember. | 0 |
| Ferryman | 4 | Once per round, you may release a member to pay its cost toward recruiting. | 0 |
| Herald of Ash | 6 | When you release a member, gain 3 ember; each rival gains 1 ember. | 0 |
| Saint of Cinders | 7 | Members you release still count as 1 follower each. | +2 |

Notes:
- **Core tension.** Kindle pays you to *hold* members; Ashes and every release space pay you to *burn* them; Vigil pays you to watch others burn. Releasing costs the member's follower (−1.5u) but Ashes refunds it as 1 follower at round end while under the cap, so a release is net-neutral on score and the space's payoff is the profit. Over the cap, releasing genuinely costs you. The cap (1/2/3) is the throttle and makes the round-III burn the climax.
- **Shape:** per-event, capped, personal (no contest). Readable from the board: each player's released-this-round count sits beside their panel as a small ash pile (cleared at round end).
- **Phoenix:** the free recruit is in addition to the turn's normal buy and comes from this sphere's stall (trial stall rule). Upgrading a 1-cost Moth into a 3-cost member is the intended line.
- **Ferryman:** a trade-in. Once per round, during any buy, release a member and count its cost as payment.
- **Saint of Cinders:** released members go face-down in an ash pile and still count as followers. It turns Conflagration into pure profit. It's the intended round-III bomb, at the top price.
- **Offered members** (if an altar sphere is on the wheel) can't be released until they return. That's a generic rule about members being away.
- **Combos (generic):** cheap members anywhere are fuel, so the Pyre competes for cheap stall members. Any sphere that rewards gaining 3+ at once or recruiting gets fed by Bonfire, Conflagration and Phoenix. Any sphere that scales with member count pulls the other way, which is good tension.
- **Risks:** (1) Saint + Conflagration + Herald in round III: release 3, gain 9 any + 9 ember, keep followers, +3 Ashes ≈ 25u from one space plus items. That's a deliberate burst, but red-team it. (2) Mourner and Vigil depend on someone releasing. Offering fills every round I, so there's usually at least 1 release, but with no other release sphere they run thin (they still have a fallback).

## Violet: The Altar (Hierophant)
Pitch: Lay it down, reap at dusk.
Verbs: offer (move your own resources or a member onto your altar), consecrate (put incense straight onto an altar)
Scoring: **The Rite**: at round end, if your altar holds 4 / 6 / 8 or more, +1 / +2 / +3 followers. Threshold, non-exclusive (everyone who clears it scores). Game max 6.
Emits: gain (incense; altar returns at round end), give (Procession puts incense on every rival's altar), buy a fixture (Great Rite, at round end), shared stake (every altar is public, and every player can clear the Rite)
Consumes: rivals buying fixtures (Cantor), resources you can't spend yet (leftovers become altar value), members as tokens (any member counts 2 on the altar)

**Altar rules** (shown on each player panel when this sphere is on the wheel):
- Altar value = resources on it, plus 2 per member.
- Altar contents still count as yours for any "hold" check, but can't be spent and members' abilities sleep.
- Offered members can't be released or swayed.
- At round end: check the Rite → resolve Great Rite purchases → everything returns to you.

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Censer | +2 incense. If your altar holds 4 or more, +2 more. |
| I | Offer | Offer up to 3 resources or 1 member; gain 1 any color. |
| I | Procession | Put 3 incense on your altar; each rival puts 1 on theirs. |
| II | Vespers | +1 incense, plus 1 per 2 on your altar. |
| II | Sanctify | Put 1 incense on your altar, then double its incense, up to +5. |
| III | Great Rite | +3 incense on your altar. Round end: it buys fixtures, each 1 cheaper. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Novice | 1 | Counts as 3 on your altar, not 2. | 0 |
| Acolyte | 2 | Round start: put 1 incense from the supply on your altar. | 0 |
| Cantor | 3 | When a rival buys a fixture, put 1 incense on your altar. | 0 |
| Thurifer | 4 | Whenever you put incense on your altar, add 1 more (once per gain). | 0 |
| Oracle | 5 | Round start: you may offer up to 3 resources, then gain 1 incense. | 0 |
| Grand Hierophant | 7 | Each round end you meet the Rite, gain 2 more followers. | +2 |

Notes:
- **Core tension.** The altar is a locked savings box. Anything on it is still yours (it comes back at round end, plus whatever incense was consecrated onto it), but you can't spend it this round. So every offer trades this round's buying power for the Rite's followers. It's the anti-Pyre: it sacrifices *tempo*, not members. Members offered come back. The sacrifice is only that their abilities sleep for the round.
- **Shape:** a personal threshold that anyone can clear. It's the opposite of a majority contest, readable at a glance (one number on each panel vs. the ring's printed 4/6/8), and never zero-sum.
- **Round-III twist:** resources are worthless after the final round, so late in round III players naturally pour leftovers onto altars to clear 8. Great Rite is the only way to turn a locked altar into fixtures at round end. That's the burst, and the race for that single space is the round-III drama.
- **Procession** is the warm space. It gives every rival real incense (it returns to them) and a nudge toward their own Rite.
- **Cantor** watches the fixture race. It links to any sphere that pushes fixture buying, and to the Diadem clock.
- **Combos (generic):**
  - Cheap members (Novice, any 1–2 cost member) are altar tokens worth 2 each.
  - A sphere that rewards holding the most of a color loves the altar, because offered resources still count as held but can't be spent away.
  - A release-heavy player and an altar-heavy player both want cheap members, which puts them in tension over stalls.
  - Thurifer + Acolyte + Sanctify is the incense engine (Sanctify caps at +5; Thurifer adds its +1 once).
- **Risks:**
  - (1) Grand Hierophant makes the Rite worth up to 3/4/5 for one player. Watch the totals.
  - (2) Procession prompts no one (automatic), but Oracle's round-start offer adds a decision at round start for its owner only.
  - (3) If the rest of the wheel is thin on fixtures early, Cantor is slow.

Lint self-check:
| ID | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | pass | Longest is 13 words |
| L2 | pass | Only generic terms: rival, fixture, member, resources, any color, round start/end. "Offer" and "altar" are this sphere's own |
| L3 | pass | No round-I space costs anything. Procession is a gift, not a toll |
| L4 | pass | No taking. Altar contents always return. Nothing goes below 0 |
| L5 | warn | Needs an altar tray on each player panel (only when this sphere is on the wheel) |
| L6 | pass | One rule: The Rite. Great Rite buys generic fixtures (market, not scoring) |
| L7 | pass | 3/2/1 spaces, 6 members, costs 1,2,3,4,5,7 |
| L8 | pass | Censer, Offer and Vespers always give ≥1–2. Sanctify floors at 2 with an empty altar |
| L9 | pass | Thurifer's extra is once per gain and doesn't retrigger. Sanctify is capped at +5 |
| L10 | pass | The Rite and Grand Hierophant pay only at round end. Great Rite's fixture buys happen at round end |

Value pass (u):
- **Censer:** 2 early, 4 with altar ≥ 4 (+33% late; scales by design). **Offer:** 1.2 + Rite progress ≈ 2.5–3. **Procession:** 3 (returns) + progress; spill to rivals 2.7, ratio 0.9.
- **Vespers:** 3–4 (altar 4–6). **Sanctify:** 2 with an empty altar; 5–6 with 2–4 incense offered.
- **Great Rite:** 3 + 1–2 discount + 1–2 extra round-end buys + rescues locked leftovers ≈ 7–8.
- **Member price as a share of EV** (bought at round-II start):
  - Novice ~45%.
  - Acolyte ~49%.
  - Cantor ~46% (rivals buy ~6 fixtures; borderline low, accepted since it's table-dependent).
  - Thurifer ~62%.
  - Oracle ~67%.
  - Grand Hierophant ~67% (3 followers + 2×2 Rite bonus).
- **Contest budget:** the Rite max 6 Favor, within 6–7. Not zero-sum, so watch whether every player clears it. Thresholds 4/6/8 make that cost two placements' worth of locked value.
- **Silo index:** ~0.6 (the altar is self-contained; Cantor, Procession and Great Rite's fixtures tie it to the table).

## Violet: The Veiled Eye (Seer)
Pitch: Foresee where rivals will go
Verbs: foretell (put a vision on a space), portent (name a color and get paid later), seek (recruit hidden members)
Scoring: Fulfillment. At round end, each of your visions that a rival took this round pays 1 / 1 / 2 followers (rings I / II / III).
Emits: mark a space; give (whoever takes a vision space gains 1); buy an item (from hidden stock)
Consumes: mark a space (anyone's marks, not just visions); rival placements on a color; round start; buy an item

Glossary (for the rules panel, not the action text):
- **Vision**: a violet marker on an empty space in any ring, including rings that haven't opened yet. When a rival places a worker there, the vision is fulfilled: you and that rival each gain 1 omen, the marker flips face-up for scoring this round, and it's removed at round end. An unfulfilled vision stays on the board into later rounds. A vision is a "marked space".
- **Later**: placed after this worker, during the same round.

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Foretell | +1 omen. Place a vision on any empty space, any ring. |
| I | Portent | +1 omen. Name a color. At round end, +1 omen per later rival there. |
| I | Read Signs | Gain 1 omen per marked space on the wheel (2 to 4). |
| II | Revelation | Place a vision, then gain 1 omen per vision you have on the wheel. |
| II | Seek | +2 omen. This turn, you may also recruit any stall's hidden next member. |
| III | Doomsday | Name a color. At round end, 2 omen per later worker there; minimum 2. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dreamer | 2 | At each round start, gain 1 omen and peek at one hidden member. | 0 |
| Star-Gazer | 3 | Portent also counts your own later workers in the named color. | 0 |
| Sign-Reader | 3 | When a rival takes any marked space, gain 1 omen. | 0 |
| Scryer | 4 | You may always recruit a stall's hidden next member instead of a face-up one. | 0 |
| Twin Sight | 5 | Foretell and Revelation each place one more vision. | 0 |
| The Blind Prophet | 7 | At each round start, place a vision. | +2 |

Notes:
- **Feel.** You predict where the table will go. Round I has 12 spaces for 12 workers, so every space fills and an early vision almost always comes true: it works as a lure (the taker gains 1), not a toll. In rounds II and III about 4 spaces stay empty at round end, so a vision is a real read. Rivals can also refuse a vision to deny your follower, at the cost of their +1. That's tension through the board, never harm. A vision placed on a ring that hasn't opened yet is a vision of next round, a delayed payoff that lands when that ring opens.
- **Timing tension.** Portent and Doomsday count only workers placed after yours, so a prophecy pays most when made early, with the least information. Whoever is last in Favor picks first, which makes these a catch-up lure. Both always pay something (Portent's +1, Doomsday's minimum of 2), so there are no dead turns.
- **Combos.**
  - Twin Sight + Revelation: a vision engine.
  - Read Signs + Sign-Reader feed off any sphere that marks spaces (sponsors, plants and so on).
  - Doomsday + any sphere that dumps workers or holds them late: the late workers land after yours and count.
  - Scryer + Seek give foresight into the market.
- **Lint self-check:**
  - L1 pass: longest effect is 14 words.
  - L2 pass: only colors, marked spaces, stalls and rivals are named.
  - L3 pass: no round-I tolls; visions are lures.
  - L4 pass: no taking.
  - L5 warn: hidden stall decks need a private peek view, and Portent and Doomsday need a color token on the player panel.
  - L6 pass: one scoring rule.
  - L7 pass: 3 / 2 / 1 spaces and 6 members.
  - L8 pass: every space has a floor (Revelation always counts the vision it just placed).
  - L9 pass: no loops; The Blind Prophet places one vision per round.
  - L10 pass: Fulfillment is tallied at round end, and Portent and Doomsday pay resources at round end.
- **Value bands** (round I / II / III):
  - Foretell: 3.4 / 2.75 / 3.4. That's 1 omen, plus the chance of fulfillment times (1 omen + the scoring value). Round I runs about 13% over the band, which is fine.
  - Portent: about 2.2 / 3 / 3.5. It scales with the number of spaces per color.
  - Read Signs: 2–4, rising as marks accumulate.
  - Revelation (round II): about 4.75.
  - Seek: about 3.3, from 2 omen plus 1–1.5u of flexibility.
  - Doomsday (round III): about 6–8, with a ceiling of about 10–12 when worker-dump effects pile into the named color. **FLAG:** watch this ceiling.
- **Spill ratio** on visions: about 0.3 (the taker's 1 against the actor's roughly 3.4).
- **Contest budget:** a focused Seer fulfills about 1 / 2 / 2.5 visions, for 1 + 2 + 5 = about 7–8 followers. That's at the top of the ≤6–7 budget. **FLAG:** if mind-play confirms it, drop round III to 1.
- **Member pricing** (follower 1.5u + 50–70% of the ability's EV; per-use numbers are from the start of round II):
  - Dreamer: EV about 2 against cost 2. **FLAG:** slightly cheap.
  - Star-Gazer: EV about 2 against cost 3.
  - Sign-Reader: EV about 4 against cost 3.
  - Scryer: about 5 buys × 0.8u, so EV about 4, against cost 4.
  - Twin Sight: 2 uses × about 2.5u, so EV about 5, against cost 5.
  - The Blind Prophet: 2 visions at about 3u, plus 3u for the 2 followers, so EV about 10.5 against cost 7 (67%).
- **Silo index:** about 0.35. Visions only pay when rivals move, and Portent and Doomsday read the table.
- **Risks:**
  - Rivals may collectively boycott visions (the rich-get-richer read), so mind-play should check whether the +1 lure is enough.
  - Hidden-member peeking is information the UI must show privately.

sphere: Amber: The Order of the Last Bell (Keeper)
spec:
## Amber: The Order of the Last Bell (Keeper)
Pitch: Strike first, or speak last
Verbs: hasten (place now), bide (place after everyone), echo (repeat your previous move)
Scoring: The Last Word. At round end, whoever placed the latest worker in this sphere this round takes 1 / 2 / 3 followers (rings I / II / III). Ties can't happen because placements are sequential.
Emits: echo; back-to-back placements and late placements (these shift the round's pace for every pace-reading effect)
Consumes: workers placed this round (anyone's); echo (rivals'); round start / round end

Glossary (for the rules panel, not the action text):
- **Wait**: the worker sits on your panel's Bell tray. After every player's last regular worker is placed, waiting workers are placed in snake order. They count as placements for every effect.
- **Skipping a turn**: the snake order is unchanged, and your seat simply passes on the turn your worker was already used for.

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Hasten | +2 sand. You may place your next worker immediately instead of on its turn. |
| I | Bide | +2 sand. Your next worker may wait, placing after everyone's last worker. |
| I | Dusk | +1 sand, plus 1 per 3 workers already placed this round. |
| II | Dawn | +2 sand, plus 1 per worker you have yet to place. |
| II | Recur | Echo your previous placement this round (not an echo); otherwise +3 sand. |
| III | Midnight | +2 sand, +1 per worker you hold; place them all now, back to back. |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Early Riser | 2 | At each round start, gain 1 sand. | 0 |
| Bell-Ringer | 3 | Dusk counts every 2 workers placed, not every 3. | 0 |
| Chronicler | 3 | When a rival echoes, gain 1 sand. | 0 |
| Sleeper | 4 | Once per round, a worker of yours may wait until the end; +1 sand. | 0 |
| Keeper of Hours | 5 | At round end, gain 1 sand per worker placed after your last one. | 0 |
| The Undying Hour | 7 | Each round, place one extra worker last of all, if a space is open. | +2 |

Notes:
- **Feel.** It's a sphere about when, not what. The snake draft stays intact: Hasten and Midnight pull your turns earlier and leave gaps, and Bide adds a final waiting phase. Nobody loses a turn they didn't choose to give up.
- **Core tension.** Dawn, Hasten and Midnight reward going early (grab contested spaces and dash). Dusk, Bide and the Last Word reward going late (read the table, have the final say). Midnight dumps all your workers early, which forfeits the Last Word. Keeper of Hours pays you to finish early, while the scoring rule pays you to finish late.
- **No round-I tolls.**
  - Dusk is a lure for the forced last picker in round I (it pays up to 4).
  - Waiting is optional, since in round I it only gets leftovers.
  - Hasten on your last worker is just +2.
- **Combos.**
  - Hasten into a strong space, then Recur to echo it.
  - Recur after any round-III center from another sphere: a big burst. **FLAG:** check this in mind-play.
  - Bide or Sleeper + a sphere that pays for later placements, or reads marks left during the round.
  - Midnight floods spaces early, which feeds any rival's "per later worker" or "marked space" effects. That's spill through the board.
- **Lint self-check:**
  - L1 pass: longest effect is 14 words.
  - L2 pass: only workers, spaces, rivals and echo are named.
  - L3 pass.
  - L4 pass: no taking.
  - L5 warn: needs a Bell tray for waiting workers and a round-placement counter on the wheel. Both are simple.
  - L6 pass.
  - L7 pass.
  - L8 pass: every space has a floor (Recur gives +3 if there's nothing to echo; Midnight gives at least +2).
  - L9 pass: Recur can't echo an echo, and echoing Midnight is impossible because you have no workers left.
  - L10 pass: the Last Word is resolved at round end; Keeper of Hours pays resources at round end.
- **Value bands** (round I / II / III):
  - Hasten: 3 (2 + 1u of tempo).
  - Bide: 2 / 3.5 / 3.5. Round I sits at the band floor on purpose, since waiting is weak while every space fills.
  - Dusk: about 2.8 / 3.5 / 4.2. It climbs because more workers are placed each round.
  - Dawn (round II): about 3.5, and about 4 in round III.
  - Recur: about 3.5–4, or about 7 when it echoes a center. **FLAG**, but it fits the round-III burst intent.
  - Midnight (round III): taken early, 6 sand + about 4u of tempo = about 10, slightly over the band (**FLAG**); taken mid-round about 6; taken late about 2–3. Taking it early is the read.
- **Contest budget:** at most 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 followers, which is within budget.
- **Member pricing** (follower 1.5u + 50–70% of the ability's EV):
  - Early Riser: EV about 1.5 against cost 2.
  - Bell-Ringer: 2–3 uses × about 1.2, so EV about 3, against cost 3.
  - Chronicler: about 3–4 rival echoes, so EV about 3.5, against cost 3. It only fires if some sphere on the wheel echoes; this sphere's own Recur guarantees one emitter.
  - Sleeper: (1.5 + 1) × 2 rounds, so EV about 5, against cost 4.
  - Keeper of Hours: about 3 per round × 2, so EV about 6, against cost 5.
  - The Undying Hour: extra leftover placements about 6u, plus 3u for the 2 followers, so EV about 10.5 against cost 7 (67%). In round I every space fills, so its extra worker usually has no space, which the "if a space is open" clause covers.
- **Silo index:** about 0.45. Dusk, Dawn and the Last Word all read the table's pace.
- **Risks:**
  - Last Word kingmaking: the seat that naturally places last (snake end) is favored. Bide and Sleeper let anyone contest it, but mind-play should check seat bias.
  - Several waiting workers resolving at the end could slow the finish. The UI should auto-prompt them in order.

## Saffron: The Wayfarers (pilgrim)
Pitch: Be everywhere; leave shrines behind.
Verbs: wander (yield scales with spheres you stand in), raise (a permanent shrine), shift (move a worker)
Scoring: The Long Road. At round end, whoever has presence in the most spheres takes 1 / 2 / 3 followers. Ties: most saffron wins; if still tied, all take. Presence means a worker or a shrine.
Emits: gain (multi-colour; 3+ at once on Journey's End), share a space (Fellowship, Wanderer), mark (shrines mark spheres), frees a space (Shift empties one mid-round), give (Innkeeper), holds the most saffron (tiebreak)
Consumes: share a space (Innkeeper), rivals' placements on inner rings (Shrine-keeper), round end (Saint), release (Acolyte)

Glossary: **Shrine**: your token on a sphere's rim; at most one per sphere per player; it stays all game. **Presence**: you have a worker or a shrine in that sphere. **Neighboring space**: a space in an adjacent sphere.

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Alms Road | +1 saffron per sphere holding your worker, this one included. (10) |
| I | Raise Shrine | +1 saffron. Raise a shrine in a sphere lacking yours; if none, +2 more. (14) |
| I | Fellowship | +2 saffron. Your next worker this round may share an occupied space. (12) |
| II | Shift | +1 saffron. Move another worker of yours to an empty neighboring space; take it. (14) |
| II | Procession | +1 saffron, plus 1 resource of each color where you're present. (11) |
| III | Journey's End | Gain 2 of each color where you're present. (8) |

| Member | Cost | Effect (≤14 words) | Extra followers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acolyte | 1 | Release it to raise a shrine. | 0 |
| Wanderer | 2 | Once per round, share an occupied space in a sphere holding your shrine. | 0 |
| Innkeeper | 3 | When a rival shares a space with you, you both gain 1 saffron. | 0 |
| Pathfinder | 4 | When you place in a sphere holding your shrine, +1 of its color. | 0 |
| Shrine-keeper | 5 | When a rival takes an inner-ring space where you have a shrine, +1 saffron. | 0 |
| Saint of the Road | 6 | Each round end, +1 follower per sphere you're present in, beyond two. | 1 |

Notes:
- **Arc.** Round I: spread thin or raise shrines. Shrines are permanent presence, so by round III your workers can stack where you like while Procession and Journey's End pay off every sphere you've touched. Journey's End with 4 spheres gives 8 resources: the burst.
- **Shift is the movement verb.** The worker it moves leaves its space empty, so a rival can take it later (a lure, never a toll). A moved worker's new space resolves normally but can never move another worker (L9). You still buy from the Saffron stall for that placement.
- **Combos.** Raise Shrine early, then Pathfinder and Shrine-keeper (shrines become income from both your own and rivals' placements). Fellowship or Wanderer into a crowded sphere, plus Innkeeper (warm: the rival you join gets paid too). Acolyte plus any release action elsewhere: a release that also builds a shrine.
- **Value pass** (u):
  - Alms Road 1–3 early (avg about 2), 3–4 late.
  - Raise Shrine 1 + about 1.5 presence equity, so about 2.5.
  - Fellowship 2 + 0.5–1, so 2.5–3.
  - Shift 1 + one extra space (about 3), so about 4.
  - Procession 1 + 2–4 off-colour, so 3.7–4.6.
  - Journey's End 6–7.4.
  - All within their ring bands; Alms Road starts at the low edge of round I and climbs.
  - Members (price ÷ ability EV, bought at the start of round II): Acolyte about 0.5u of net ability (fodder); Wanderer EV 1.5, price ≈ 2.4; Innkeeper EV 2.5, ≈ 3.0; Pathfinder EV about 5 (about 5 triggers), ≈ 4.5; Shrine-keeper EV 6–7 (about 7 rival inner placements × 0.5 shrine coverage), ≈ 5.5, so slightly cheap at 5; Saint EV about 4 followers + 1 extra = 7.5u, ≈ 6.0.
  - Silo index about 0.6. Spill ratio: Innkeeper 1.0. Contest total 6 followers, within the cap.
- **Lints.** L1 pass: the longest effect is 14 words. L2 pass. L3 pass. L4 pass (no takes). L5 warn: shrines need a rim slot per sphere. L6 pass. L7 pass. L8 warn: Shift on your first worker of a round gives only +1 saffron. L9 pass: a moved worker never moves another. L10 pass: Long Road and Saint pay out at round end.
- **Risks.**
  - In round III, presence saturates at 4 spheres, so the Long Road tiebreak (saffron) decides often. That's acceptable as seasoning, but watch it.
  - Saint in a 4-sphere engine yields 6 followers for 6u, near Diadem efficiency but conditional. Flag it for the red team.
  - Shift opens a space mid-round; the UI must highlight newly empty spaces.

## Ivory: The Reliquary (curator)
Pitch: Covet, unveil, and anoint members.
Verbs: reserve (set a stall member aside for yourself), refresh (redeal a stall), recruit (extra and discounted buys); also uses the generic verb release
Scoring: The Fold. At round end, whoever recruited the most members this round takes 1 / 2 / 3 followers. Ties all take. Reserving doesn't count; recruiting from the reserve does.
Emits: buy an item (lots of it, often 2–3 per turn late), buys from any stall, refresh (new stall members for everyone), release (members return to their decks), gain (Tithe)
Consumes: rivals' expensive recruits (Watcher), member count (Tithe, Hierophant, Zealot), its own recruit tally (Prophet), release (Relinquish)

Glossary: **Reserve**: move a stall member onto your panel; at most 2 at a time; the stall refills at once; you alone may recruit it with any later buy. **Refresh**: put a stall's members under its deck and deal 2 new ones. **Release**: discard your member to the bottom of its deck; you lose its follower.

| Ring | Action | Effect (≤14 words) |
|---|---|---|
| I | Tithe | +1 ivory per member you own: at least 2, at most 5. (11) |

Notes:
- **Arc.** Round I: Covet the member you want and Unveil stalls to find cheap ones; Tithe pays more as your following grows. Round II: Induction gives you two recruits in one turn, and Relinquish turns old members back into cash (plus another shot at the Fold). Round III: Anoint is a free member, possibly a 7. Prophet and Hierophant turn the round-III shopping spree into the burst. This sphere makes a table explosive (S7): a high score scale.
- **The market is the board here.** Covet denies a member to everyone else, Unveil reshuffles what everyone can buy, and Watcher makes you root for rivals' big buys. Released members go back to the bottom of their deck, so they come round again.
- **Combos.** Covet early, then Almoner, then Anoint pulls the reserved 7-cost for free. Zealot + Tithe/Hierophant (and any other sphere's per-member scaling). Steward + Induction: cheap double recruits that win the Fold. Relinquish an Acolyte-style member whose release ability fires too.
- **Value pass** (u):
  - Tithe 2 early, 3–5 late (capped).
  - Covet 1 + about 1.5 (flex and denial), so 2.5.
  - Unveil 1 + 0.5 info + 1 any-stall, so 2.5.
  - Induction 1 discount + 1 flex + about 1.5–2 extra-buy equity, so 3.5–4.
  - Relinquish 3 flat, or cost + 2 − 1.5 (a 4-cost gives 4.5).
  - Anoint: average member about 4u + flex + Fold equity, so 6–8.
  - All within their ring bands.
  - Members (price ≈ 1.5 + 0.6 × ability EV): Zealot about 1, ≈ 2.1, so 1 is fodder; Almoner 1.5, ≈ 2.4; Watcher about 3 triggers, ≈ 3.3; Steward about 4.5, ≈ 4.2; Hierophant 3–4 followers for an ivory player (about 5u), ≈ 4.5–5; Prophet about 4 followers + 1 extra = 7.5u, ≈ 6.0 (73%, the upper edge).
  - Silo index about 0.5 (stalls are shared). Contest total 6 followers.
- **Lints.** L1 pass: the longest is 14 words. L2 pass. L3 pass. L4 pass. L5 warn: the reserve needs 2 panel slots and the per-round recruit tally needs a counter. L6 pass. L7 pass. L8 warn: Induction gives nothing extra if you can't afford a member. L9 pass: no repeat chains; Steward and Almoner have floors; Anoint is a single recruit. L10 pass: Fold, Hierophant and Prophet pay at round end.
- **Risks.**
  - In round III, Prophet + Anoint + Induction can bank 5+ followers in one round. That's intended as the burst, but the red team should price the ceiling.
  - The recruit-then-Relinquish loop pumps the Fold tally; it's bounded by placements and costs a follower each time.
  - Covet can hate-draft a rival's needed member; there's a cap of 2 reserved.
